newsitem.title: USA: IBP sees increased interest from Japan.
newsitem.headline: IBP sees increased interest from Japan.

text.p: Meat processor IBP Inc said it has received increased interest in its pork products from Japan, after Taiwan banned its pork exports due to a disease outbreak in that country.
Taiwan is the top supplier of pork to Japan. Taiwanese pork supplies have been affected by an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in the hog herd in Taiwan.
"We have seen increased interest in our product from Japanese customers," IBP spokesman Gary Mickelsen said. "But what it will mean long term will be difficult to say."
Japan is currently IBP's largest customer for both beef and pork.

In 1996, IBP's total worldwide exports amounted to $1.7 billion, or 13 percent of its total net sales for the year of $12.5 billion. Exports in 1996 were down eight percent from the record level of 1995 but were still the second-highest in the company's history, IBP said in January.

Earlier this week, Glenn Grimes, an agricultural economist at the University of Missouri, forecasted that the United States would gain two-thirds of Taiwan's share of the Japanese pork export market. In 1996, Taiwan exported 335,000 tonnes of pork to Japan, he said.
